q: Why is photolysis said to be 'driven' by photosystem II?
options: Light energy directly breaks the O–H bonds of water molecules dissolved in the stroma, releasing O2
ATP made by PSI provides the energy needed to split water molecules in the lumen
After losing an electron, P680+ is a strong enough oxidising agent to pull electrons from water
Reduced NADP donates energy to the water molecules, causing them to split apart
explanation: After P680 emits an excited electron, the oxidised P680+ has an extremely high affinity for electrons – it is the strongest biological oxidising agent known – strong enough to remove electrons from water (via the manganese cluster), which normally holds them very tightly. So light doesn't split water directly; the electron 'hole' left in PSII does.
